sources.source_title: EPEX SPOT Fees page and New Price List Guide (public)
sources.notes: The public Fees page and the downloadable Price List Guide describe Market Access, Flat Trading Fees, and Technical Add-ons qualitatively and direct readers to sales@epexspot.com. No current €/MWh or annual membership figure is printed in those public documents (retrieved 2026-11-10). The sourced per-MWh preset therefore does not include an EPEX trading-fee component. This is a lower bound on total exchange costs if a member still pays a trading fee. Guide PDF: https://www.epexspot.com/sites/default/files/download_center_files/New%20Price%20List%20Guide.pdf

sources.value: DA DE-AT-CH 0.04; FR DA 0.07; ID 0.10 (2015 list)
sources.source_title: EPEX SPOT Price List valid 1 January 2015 (unofficial host; stale)
sources.notes: Historical public list only, retrieved for context. Entrance 25,000 €; annual one/two/three market access 10,000 / 20,000 / 30,000 €; ETS Standard 8,000 € / Light 3,500 €. These are not current official rates and are not used in the sourced preset. They informed the earlier ASSUMED 0.05 €/MWh order-of-magnitude (A-C1).

sources.item: ECC Lux clearing fee — Power Day-ahead Spot trades
sources.source_title: ECC Price List, Document Release 085b, 02.11.2026, §4.1 Power spot
sources.notes: Official current price list (English information version; German legally binding), publishing date 2 November 2026, linked from https://www.ecc.de/en/rules-regulations/rules. Standard rate 0.015 €/MWh for Power Day-ahead Spot trades (ECC Lux). Exceptions (Serbia/Slovenia 0.020, Ireland, GB) do not apply to DE-LU. Baltic DA auction waiver is also not DE-LU. This is the only variable €/MWh figure in the sourced DA fee preset.

sources.item: ECC Lux clearing fee — Power Intraday Spot / SIDC IDAs
sources.notes: 0.035 €/MWh for Power Intraday Spot trades; footnote *4 states the same rate applies to Pan-European Intraday Auctions (IDAs). Documented for completeness. The current paper model is day-ahead only, so this rate is not added to the sourced DA ExecutionCosts preset.

sources.item: ECC membership fees (fixed, not converted to €/MWh)
sources.value: NCM 1,000 € p.a.; Institution CM 12,500 € p.a.; DCP Power Markets Plus 12,500 € p.a.
sources.notes: Non-Clearing Member 1,000 € p.a. (clearing-fee credit against the membership fee; first 12 months waived). Institution Clearing Member 12,500 € p.a. (first 12 months waived). DCP Power Markets Plus 12,500 € p.a. (or 11,000 £ if GBP power only). Technical access EUREX GUI via public Internet 7,500 € p.a. (not applicable to DCP). Fixed fees are disclosed here and are not amortised into the per-MWh sourced preset: any €/MWh conversion would depend on annual throughput and membership type (modelling choice, not a published tariff).

sources.item: Nord Pool variable DA fees (Nordic/Baltic 2026 schedule; NEMO comparator, not EPEX DE-LU)
sources.source_title: Nord Pool AS Fee Schedule, Nordic / Baltic Market, effective 1 January 2026
sources.notes: Official PDF retrieved 2026-11-10. Section 1.4: Day-ahead market trading 0.040 €/MWh and clearing 0.015 €/MWh (combined 0.055); small participant DA 0.125+0.015=0.140; intraday continuous 0.109+0.015=0.124; SIDC IDA 0.060+0.015=0.075. Annual participant access DA+ID continuous: 21,500 € (additional area 11,000 €); small participant can waive the annual fee and pay the higher variable rate (floors apply). Note (b) lists Germany/Luxembourg among the areas used for the 65,000 € annual access-fee cap when applying for multiple Nord Pool areas. The document title is 'Nordic / Baltic Market'; a separate public CWE/DE-LU fee schedule was not found at retrieval. These rates are a published NEMO comparator, not a substitute for the unpublished current EPEX DE-LU trading fee, and they are not added to the sourced ExecutionCosts preset.

sources.item: German grid-access charges (Netzentgelte) for eligible electricity storage
sources.notes: Official text: installations for storing electrical energy newly built after 31 December 2008 and commissioned from 4 August 2011 within 18 years (i.e. by 4 August 2029) are exempt for 20 years from commissioning from grid-access charges (Entgelte für den Netzzugang) on energy withdrawn for storage, provided the energy is taken from a transmission or distribution grid and the recovered energy is fed back into the same grid. The exemption does not automatically cover every levy or concession fee. For the illustrative 1 MW / 2 MWh paper asset, assumed commissioned in the exemption window and same-grid, the sourced preset applies 0 €/MWh grid-access charge on stored energy. This is a legal condition, not a published TSO tariff table.

sources.unit: EUR/MWh (quarter-hourly, published, not a fixed tariff)
sources.notes: reBAP is a published quarter-hourly settlement price for balance-group imbalances, not a fixed €/MWh trading fee. It can be positive or negative. The current paper model is day-ahead only and settles planned DA volumes at the DA clearing price, so no imbalance volume is simulated and no reBAP charge is applied. A live physical asset would face reBAP on residual imbalances.

sources.item: Day-ahead slippage / bid-ask (SDAC single clearing price)
sources.source_title: Market design: SDAC day-ahead auction (single clearing price per MTU)
sources.notes: The coupled day-ahead auction produces one clearing price per market time unit. There is no classic bid-ask spread on a filled DA auction trade. The sourced DA preset therefore sets slippage to 0 (pure auction-fill paper assumption). The previous 0.50 €/MWh figure remains an ASSUMED conservatism (A-C2) in the assumed preset, not a published fee.

sources.source_title: NREL/NLR 2025 Annual Technology Baseline — Utility-Scale Battery Storage (context only; no published €/MWh wear tariff)
sources.notes: No public exchange or TSO document publishes a battery degradation tariff in €/MWh. NREL/NLR ATB 2025 (LFP utility-scale, retrieved 2026-11-10) states a 15-year technical life, approximately one cycle per day, variable O&M of zero, and fixed O&M at 4% of capital cost in $/kW including augmentation so the system can hold rated capacity over that life (Cole et al., 2025). A primary-source 2024 overnight $/kWh table was not successfully retrieved this day (NREL PDF TLS failure), so no €/MWh figure is derived here. The sourced preset therefore keeps the existing ASSUMED 5 €/MWh throughput wear proxy (A-C3; Kies et al. 2018 DOI 10.1088/1742-6596/977/1/012005 is order-of-magnitude framing only).

Baselines reuse prior gross (deg=0) dumps and the same accounting layer for the selected preset
Tight Mondrian: hour-bucket × hourly residual-load tercile × 7d/60d hour volatility, with parent fallback
